reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) only describes hot corrosion performance and oxide composition (Al2O3, Cr2O3, spinels) for AlCoCrFeNi2.1 high-entropy alloy coatings at 900 °C, not for Q235 steel. None of the key premises about annealing Q235 steel, forming Fe-oxide scales, or linking scale properties to dual-environment corrosion protection are supported by the provided passages.
premises: Annealing Q235 steel at 800 °C can form a continuous, adherent oxide scale
The oxide scale will be predominantly protective Fe-oxides and minor spinels
An optimal oxide scale acts as a barrier to aggressive species in both molten salt and aqueous environments
Deviations in annealing time lead to insufficient or overgrown/unstable scales
The oxide scale properties directly control corrosion performance in both high-temperature and room-temperature regimes
